trust_decision.summary: On the LDAPS and StartTLS paths the client trusts the TLS peer's certificate chain (via the configured TrustManagers) but makes no decision about whether the certificate's identity matches the configured LDAP host: addSslFilter builds the MINA SslFilter/SSLContext with no endpoint identification algorithm.

landing_point.why: It is the only place in the tree that builds an SslFilter/SSLContext for the client (grep for SslFilter and SSLContext returns this method alone), so anyone reading 'LDAP API lacks server certificate verification for LDAP hostnames' lands here.

fix_sites.entry_point: LdapNetworkConnection.connect() (LDAPS, config.isUseSsl()) and LdapNetworkConnection.startTls() (public, and auto-invoked from connect() when config.isUseTls())
fix_sites.module_kind: client connection handler / MINA filter-chain setup

fix_sites.entry_point: LdapConnectionConfig public getter/setter (constructor default applied to every LdapNetworkConnection built from host/port or from a config)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can leave the user-supplied plain X509TrustManager path alone: the caller installed its own TrustManager (and the API itself ships NoVerificationTrustManager to opt out of verification), so certificate identity reads as 'the TrustManager's job', not the connection's.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: NoVerificationTrustManager is a public X509ExtendedTrustManager whose checkServerTrusted is a no-op; the published fix's own test asserts the handshake must still SUCCEED against a certificate whose CN does not match the host when that trust manager is configured. An over-broad fix that verifies the peer certificate name itself in addSslFilter (instead of leaving the decision to JSSE/SSLParameters) breaks that documented opt-out, and LdapConnectionConfigTest already asserts the class is accepted as a TrustManager.

O6_input_shapes: null value on the same setter, which is the documented opt-out from hostname verification
any other SSLParameters endpoint-identification string passed through the setter unchanged
both TLS establishment modes: LDAPS from connect()/createConnector (config.isUseSsl()) and StartTLS from startTls()/config.isUseTls()

O8_uncovered_routes.route: A TrustManager[] installed through LdapConnectionConfig.setTrustManagers, where the element is a plain javax.net.ssl.X509TrustManager (the API's own LdapClientTrustStoreManager is one) rather than an X509ExtendedTrustManager: addSslFilter still sets the endpoint identification algorithm, but JSSE only performs the identity check inside an X509ExtendedTrustManager, so the handshake with a mismatched certificate name still succeeds.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The trust manager was supplied by the caller, the class is documented as a trust-store loader that deliberately lets self-signed certificates through, and the advisory is about the connection not setting the algorithm - which the fix now does.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Same package; 1 file from addSslFilter (LdapNetworkConnection.java:5093) and never referenced by the connection code.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An identity check inside the API's own trust manager (make it an X509ExtendedTrustManager or verify the peer name after the chain check)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This class exists precisely to validate the LDAP server chain for TLS/SSL, its javadoc says it is used during JSSE certificate validation, and a maintainer fixing CWE-297 would plausibly harden the trust manager itself once they noticed SSLParameters cannot reach plain trust managers.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Normalise the configured TrustManager[] at SSLContext.init by wrapping plain X509TrustManagers in an X509ExtendedTrustManager that performs the endpoint check
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the single SSLContext.init site, so wrapping there is the natural place to make the new algorithm effective for every trust manager the API accepts.

O9_family: improper certificate validation: missing TLS server-identity (hostname) verification in an LDAP client (CWE-297)

O10_build.toolchain: Maven multi-module (i18n, util, asn1, all, ldap, dsml, integ, integ-osgi, distribution), maven.compiler 1.8; ldap/client/api depends on mina-core 2.2.5, commons-pool2, slf4j and JUnit 5
O10_build.project_tests: No TLS or hostname-verification test exists at the pinned commit; the fix adds LdapNetworkConnectionSslTest (in-memory BouncyCastle cert plus a loopback SSLServerSocket, no external server). LdapNetworkConnectionTest only computes timeouts and never connects.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add sslFilter.setEndpointIdentificationAlgorithm( "LDAPS" ) hardcoded inside addSslFilter, or verify the peer certificate name by hand in addSslFilter, and stop there.

unverified: The claim that JSSE skips endpoint identification for a plain X509TrustManager (sun.security.ssl AbstractTrustManagerWrapper delegates without an identity check) is JSSE behaviour, not visible in this tree; it was reasoned, not executed. It is what makes the O8 route real.
Repo source size in MB could not be measured (no shell available), so tiny_repo/giant_repo were judged only from the tree shape (about 1500 main Java files across 9 modules).
Whether MINA 2.2.5 actually exposes SslFilter.setEndpointIdentificationAlgorithm (used by the fix) could not be checked; the mina jar is not in the tree and no network was used.
The fix's added test dependency (bcpkix-jdk18on via a new bouncycastle.version property) was not built, so offline build of the test module was not confirmed.
